message.content:
### Building a New PC – Step‑by‑Step Guide

Below is a practical, beginner‑friendly walkthrough.  
Feel free to skip sections you already know, but keep the safety and order in mind.

| # | What to Do | Why It Matters | Tips |
|---|------------|----------------|------|
| 1 | **Plan & Budget** | Know what you’ll use it for (gaming, video editing, office, etc.) | Use PCPartPicker.com to check compatibility and price. |
| 2 | **Gather Tools & Workspace** | A clean, static‑free area keeps components safe. | 1‑2 screwdrivers (Phillips & flathead), anti‑static wrist strap, cable ties, a large table or desk. |
| 3 | **Choose Components** | CPU, GPU, motherboard, RAM, storage, PSU, case, cooling. | Stick to the same brand family (e.g., Intel or AMD) for easier compatibility. |
| 4 | **Read Manuals** | Each component has quirks. | Keep the motherboard manual handy for BIOS settings. |
| 5 | **Prepare the Case** | Remove side panels, install standoffs. | Use the case’s standoff kit; align with motherboard holes. |
| 6 | **Install the Power Supply (PSU)** | Provides power to all parts. | Mount it at the bottom or top (depending on case). Connect the 24‑pin ATX and 8‑pin CPU power cables to the motherboard. |
| 7 | **Mount the Motherboard** | The foundation of your build. | Align the I/O shield with the case’s back panel. Screw the motherboard into the standoffs. |
| 8 | **Install the CPU** | The brain of the system. | Open the CPU socket latch, place the CPU (look for the corner triangle), lock the latch. |
| 9 | **Apply Thermal Paste & Install CPU Cooler** | Prevents overheating. | If the cooler comes with paste, use a pea‑size amount. Secure the cooler with the mounting bracket. |
|10 | **Insert RAM** | Determines multitasking speed. | Snap sticks into the correct slots (usually the second slot for dual‑channel). |
|11 | **Mount Storage (SSD/HDD)** | Where your OS and files live. | Use 2.5″ or 3.5″ mounting brackets or drive cages. |
|12 | **Install the GPU** | Graphics card for gaming or rendering. | Insert into the top PCI‑e x16 slot, secure with screws, connect 6‑/8‑pin PCI‑e power cables from PSU. |
|13 | **Connect Front Panel & USB Headers** | Power button, LEDs, USB ports work. | Refer to motherboard manual for pin layout. |
|14 | **Cable Management** | Keeps airflow and looks tidy. | Route cables behind the motherboard tray, use ties or Velcro straps. |
|15 | **Double‑Check Connections** | Avoid shorts or power issues. | Verify all power connectors, data cables, and that no screws are loose. |
|16 | **Power On & Enter BIOS** | First boot to confirm hardware. | Press the power button; if the fan spins and you see the BIOS screen, you’re good. |
|17 | **Update BIOS (if needed)** | Compatibility with newer CPUs or GPUs. | Download the latest BIOS from the motherboard manufacturer’s site. |
|18 | **Install Operating System** | Windows, Linux, etc. | Create a bootable USB with Rufus or similar, boot from it, and follow the installer. |
|19 | **Install Drivers & Updates** | Optimal performance and stability. | Start with chipset, GPU, audio, network drivers. |
|20 | **Test & Benchmark** | Ensure everything runs smoothly. | Run stress tests (Prime95, FurMark) and benchmark tools (Cinebench, 3DMark). |

---

#### Quick Component Checklist

| Category | Typical Choices | Notes |
|----------|-----------------|-------|
| **CPU** | Intel i5/i7/i9, AMD Ryzen 5/7/9 | Match socket with motherboard. |
| **Motherboard** | B550 / X570 (AMD), B460 / Z490 (Intel) | Ensure it supports your CPU and has enough PCI‑e slots. |
| **RAM** | 16GB DDR4 (3200‑3600MHz) | Dual‑channel for best performance. |
| **GPU** | RTX 3060 / RTX 3070 / RX 6700 XT | Depends on budget and resolution. |
| **Storage** | NVMe SSD (500GB‑2TB) | Fast boot and load times. |
| **PSU** | 650W‑750W 80+ Gold | Sufficient headroom for future upgrades. |
| **Case** | Mid‑tower ATX | Good airflow, cable management space. |
| **Cooling** | Stock cooler (if included) or aftermarket AIO | Consider 240‑mm or 280‑mm for better temps. |

---

#### Safety & Tips

- **Static Electricity**: Ground yourself with an anti‑static wrist strap or touch a metal part of the case before handling components.
- **Cable Management**: Use Velcro ties or zip ties; keep cables away from fans.
- **BIOS Settings**: Enable XMP for RAM, set boot priority to your SSD, disable unused onboard devices if you’re using discrete ones.
- **Thermal Paste**: A pea‑size amount is usually enough; too much can be counterproductive.
- **Documentation**: Keep the manuals for each component; they’re invaluable for troubleshooting.

---

#### Common Pitfalls

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| **PC doesn’t power on** | Check PSU switch, ensure all power connectors are seated, verify that the motherboard standoffs are correctly installed. |
| **No display** | Confirm GPU is seated, power cables are connected, and the monitor is set to the correct input. |
| **Overheating** | Reapply thermal paste, improve cable routing, add case fans. |
| **Component incompatibility** | Use PCPartPicker’s “Check Compatibility” feature before buying. |

---

#### Final Words

Building a PC is a rewarding experience that gives you control over performance, aesthetics, and future upgrades. Take your time, double‑check every connection, and enjoy the process! If you hit a snag, feel free to ask for help—happy building!
